walkthroughs.body_html:
Applied Anatomy and Physiology — a core area of GCSE PE.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Applied Anatomy and Physiology brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Applied Anatomy and Physiology.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: How many bones are in the adult human skeleton?

options: Elbow
Knee
Hip
Wrist

mcqs.q: Which of these is a ball-and-socket joint?
options: The knee.
The elbow.
The hip (and the shoulder).
Muscle to muscle.
Muscle to bone.
Muscle to muscle.
The knee.
Bone to bone, stabilising a joint.

mcqs.q: What type of joint is the knee?
options: Muscle to muscle.
A ball-and-socket joint.
A fixed, immovable joint.
A hinge joint, allowing flexion and extension.

sequence.def: The whole bony framework of the body.
Skull, spine and ribs — the central division.
Limbs and girdles — the outer division.
Where two bones meet, allowing movement.
A freely movable joint, e.g. the knee.
Tough tissue connecting bone to bone at a joint.
